ai.description: The Southern Bronzeback reaches 1.5m. It features a bronze-brown dorsum, a yellow-green lateral stripe, and exceptionally large eyes. A black postocular stripe extends onto the neck.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Dendrelaphis grandoculis* is the presence of a distinct, broad black stripe running through the eye and continuing along the neck.
ai.habitat: The Southern Bronzeback inhabits evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at mid-to-high altitudes between 600 and 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Southern Bronzeback is a diurnal, arboreal snake that actively hunts lizards and frogs among tree branches and foliage during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Dendrelaphis grandoculis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Dendrelaphis grandoculis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, occurring in states like Kerala, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka at elevations up to 1,200 meters.
